\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.LearningAndTesting.DerandomizedBLRProgram}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Boolean and binary field equivalence]
\lean{FABL.boolF₂Equiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
The set of Boolean values is equivalent to the field with two elements,
$\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean vector and binary cube equivalence]
\lean{FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.boolF₂Equiv}
For each natural number $n$, the set of Boolean vectors of length $n$ is equivalent to
the set of length-$n$ vectors over the field with two elements.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Random bit vector program]
\lean{FABL.randomBitVectorProgram}
\label{FABL.randomBitVectorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.map}
For each dimension $d$ and length $m$, this program uses $m$ unbiased coin tosses to
produce a Boolean vector of length $m$; it runs in the query-access model for dimension
$d$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform distribution on an empty function space]
\lean{FABL.uniformPMF_finZeroArrowBool}
\label{FABL.uniformPMF_finZeroArrowBool}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
The uniform distribution on the set of functions from the empty set to
$\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ is concentrated on the unique empty function.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform output of random bit vectors]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_randomBitVectorProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_randomBitVectorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningCost.coin, FABL.LearningCost.toTriple_injective, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_map, FABL.map_uniformPMF_equiv, FABL.randomBitVectorProgram, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformPMF_bind_map_pair, FABL.uniformPMF_finZeroArrowBool}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^{n}\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean
function. Running the program that generates $b$ independent unbiased bits and records
its work cost gives the uniform distribution on vectors in $\{0,1\}^{b}$, paired with
the fixed cost $(0,0,b)$ (zero random examples, zero queries, and $b$ units of work).
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[BLR linearity decision]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding}
Given a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube over the two-element field and
inputs $x,y$, this decision returns true exactly when the function's encoded values
satisfy $f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR query program]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRQueryProgram}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRQueryProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binarySignEquiv}
For each $n$ and inputs $x,y$ in the $n$-dimensional cube over the two-element field,
this query-access program queries the target at the sign-embedded inputs corresponding
to $x$, $y$, and $x+y$, then returns whether the decoded answers satisfy the linearity
equation $f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Outcome of the three-query BLR test]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRQueryProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRQueryProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision, FABL.derandomizedBLRQueryProgram}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let
$x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Running the three-query BLR program with target $f$ has
probability-one outcome equal to true exactly when $F(x)+F(y)=F(x+y)$, where $F$ is the
binary encoding of $f$; its cost is $(0,3,3)$ (random examples, queries, and local work,
respectively).
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[BLR local work]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork}
\leanok
For each $n$, the local-work count is $2n+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR learning cost]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRCost}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork}
For each $n$ and $r$, the learning cost has zero random-example calls, three membership
queries, and local work $n+r+(2n+1)+3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Random-bit count]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRRandomBits}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRRandomBits}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the quantity defined by this function is $n+r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR program after choosing an input]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.bind, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork, FABL.derandomizedBLRQueryProgram, FABL.randomBitVectorProgram}
Let $n$ and $r$ be natural numbers, let a seed map send each $r$-bit string to an
element of $(
\mathbb F_2)^n$, and let $x$ be an $n$-bit input. The resulting query program samples an
$r$-bit string uniformly, incurs the specified local-work charge, and then runs the
query procedure using the encoding of $x$ and the seed map’s output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Derandomized BLR program]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.LearningProgram.bind, FABL.derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram, FABL.randomBitVectorProgram}
Let $n$ and $r$ be natural numbers, and let a seed map send each $r$-bit string to an
element of $(\mathbb F_2)^n$. The associated query program runs the input-stage program
with this seed map and then samples an independent uniform $n$-bit input.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Derandomized BLR decision result]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramResult}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramResult}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision}
Let $n$ and $r$ be natural numbers, let the target be a function from the
$n$-dimensional Boolean cube to $\{-1,1\}$, let a seed map send each $r$-bit string to
$(\mathbb F_2)^n$, and let $(x,s)$ consist of an $n$-bit string and an $r$-bit string.
The result is the Boolean output of the derandomized BLR decision procedure applied to
the target, the encoding of $x$, and the seed map’s value at $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cost of the ticked three-query test]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRTickQueryProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRTickQueryProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningCost.toTriple_injective, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision, FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork, FABL.derandomizedBLRQueryProgram, FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRQueryProgram}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let
$x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Running the three-query BLR program after charging $2n+1$ local
computation steps has probability-one outcome equal to true exactly when
$F(x)+F(y)=F(x+y)$, where $F$ is the binary encoding of $f$; its cost is $(0,3,2n+1+3)$
(random examples, queries, and local work, respectively).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cost law for the derandomized BLR program]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_bind, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision, FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork, FABL.derandomizedBLRQueryProgram, FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRTickQueryProgram, FABL.runWithCost_randomBitVectorProgram, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,r\ge0$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb F_2^n$ be a
seed map, and fix an input $b\in\{0,1\}^n$. Running the program that first draws a
uniform seed, then tests the BLR relation using three queries to $f$ and charges $2n+1$
local work steps has the following joint law of output and cost: the seed is uniform on
$\{0,1\}^r$, the output is the BLR decision on the corresponding binary inputs, and the
cost is always $(0,3,r+(2n+1)+3)$, recording respectively random examples, queries, and
work.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Outcome law and cost of the derandomized BLR program]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningCost.toTriple_injective, FABL.LearningProgram.addOutcomeCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost_bind, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram, FABL.derandomizedBLRCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision, FABL.derandomizedBLRLocalWork, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramResult, FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRAfterInputProgram, FABL.runWithCost_randomBitVectorProgram, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformPMF_bind_map_pair}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let
$s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a seed map. When the derandomized BLR program runs
with target $f$, its joint law of output and cost is the law obtained by choosing
independent uniform bit vectors $u\in\{0,1\}^n$ and $v\in\{0,1\}^r$, returning the BLR
test result on the corresponding cube point and seed point, and assigning cost
$(0,3,n+r+(2n+1)+3)$ (random examples, queries, and local work, respectively).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cost of supported program outcomes]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram_cost_eq_of_mem_support}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram_cost_eq_of_mem_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram, FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRProgram}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r$ be nonnegative integers, let the target be a Boolean function on the sign
cube, and let the seed map send Boolean strings of length $r$ to the binary cube of
dimension $n$. Every outcome in the support of the program’s run distribution has cost
$(0,3,n+r+(2n+1)+3)$: zero random examples, three membership queries, and $n+r+(2n+1)+3$
units of local work.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Program resource bounds]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram_resources_of_mem_support}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r$ be nonnegative integers, let the target be a Boolean function on the sign
cube, and let the seed map send Boolean strings of length $r$ to the binary cube of
dimension $n$. Every outcome in the support of the program’s run distribution uses zero

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance for a linear target]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRProgram_eq_pure_of_isF₂Linear}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsF₂Linear, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.blrAccepts, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.derandomizedBLRCost, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgram, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramResult, FABL.runWithCost_derandomizedBLRProgram}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let
$s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a seed map. If the binary encoding
$F:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ of $f$ satisfies $F(x+y)=F(x)+F(y)$ for all
$x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, then the derandomized BLR program has the deterministic outcome
true and cost $(0,3,n+r+(2n+1)+3)$ with probability one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Derandomized BLR acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramAcceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramResult}
Let $n$ and $r$ be natural numbers, let the target be a function from the
$n$-dimensional Boolean cube to the signs, and let a seed map send each $r$-bit string
to $(\mathbb F_2)^n$. The acceptance probability is the expectation, over independent
uniform $n$-bit and $r$-bit strings, of the indicator that the derandomized BLR decision
procedure accepts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability identity]
\lean{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramAcceptanceProbability_eq}
\label{FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramAcceptanceProbability_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_uniformPushforward, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.uniformPushforward, FABL.blrAccepts, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.booleanFunctionF₂Encoding, FABL.derandomizedBLRAcceptanceProbability, FABL.derandomizedBLRDecision, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramAcceptanceProbability, FABL.derandomizedBLRProgramResult}
\difficulty{5}
For every target Boolean function on the sign cube and every seed map from Boolean seed
strings to the binary cube, the program’s acceptance probability equals the derandomized
BLR acceptance probability of the encoded target under the probability density induced
by the seed map.
\end{theorem}
